articles.title: A “Scheme” Against Dobbs: SCOTUS Dissent Hints at Next Phase of Abortion Rights Fight
articles.summary: Cisco drops another CVSS 10.0 SD-WAN zero-day getting pwned in the wild — because apparently once wasn't enough for these networking wizards. CISA is practically screaming at federal agencies to patch this perfection of a vulnerability.

articles.title: Microsoft Reports Severe Zero-Day Flaw in On-Prem Exchange Servers
articles.summary: Microsoft's on-prem Exchange servers are getting roasted via crafted emails exploiting CVE-2026-42897, a delicious XSS-to-RCE chain. Because nothing says 'enterprise security' like your email server becoming someone else's playground.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch bonanza delivers 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the delightfully named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender bug. Meanwhile Chrome squashes its fourth zero-day of the year because browsers are basically Swiss cheese at this point.

articles.title: MPs want social media treated more like unsafe toys than harmless apps
articles.summary: OpenAI employees got their devices compromised via poisoned npm packages in the TanStack supply chain attack — proving even AI overlords fall for classic software distribution tricks. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a backdoor.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas learning platform gets ransomed harder than a suburban mom's minivan, disrupting education nationwide with login page graffiti. Millions of students suddenly discover there are worse things than pop quizzes.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram officially murders its barely-used end-to-end encryption feature, breaking years-old promises to users. Meta continues its proud tradition of privacy theater followed by quiet capitulation to surveillance capitalism.

articles.title: EFF Launches New Offline Campaign for Saudi Wikipedian Osama Khalid
articles.summary: Victory lap time: Apple finally enables encrypted RCS messaging with Android, meaning your cross-platform gossip stays private by default. Only took them approximately forever, but hey, better late than surveilled.

articles.title: Turla Turns Kazuar Backdoor Into Modular P2P Botnet for Persistent Access
articles.summary: Linux kernel serves up 'Fragnesia' — a fresh root-level privilege escalation bug with public exploit code attached like a bow on a present. Memory handling bugs continue their victory tour through enterprise infrastructure.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SMS phishing his way through corporate America. Another script kiddie learns that cybercrime doesn't actually pay when the FBI comes knocking.

articles.title: OpenLoop Health confirms January 2026 Data breach affecting 716,000
articles.summary: Congress wants answers after Canvas hack exposed 9,000+ schools to data thieves exploiting Instructure's shoddy security. The House Homeland Security Committee finally wakes up to discover that EdTech is a privacy nightmare.
